text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Lebanon warns against the collapse of peace in the region and says it will support an extension of term for the U.N. secretary-general.
-U.S. and French ambassadors visited Prime Minister Hariri. Jones: Lebanon will not be affected by the latest developments in the region.
-Israeli planes flew over most of the south and the capital and Israeli artillery shelled the eastern and central sector of the south.
-MP Nassib Lahoud: I hope the role of the new parliament is not only to provide automatic cover up for the government.
-Cabinet meets today to discuss the media law.
-Beirut Secondary Market closed after SOLIDERE shares moved to the official Beirut Stock Exchange.
-The European Union launches projects to modernise public administration in Lebanon.
-Minister of Health Hamade: We have closed all illegal pharmacies across Lebanon.
-Hizbollah launched 826 attacks in nine months killing 23 Israelis and wounding 180.
